| KS-E1AP-D1 | 2026-10-15 | The CU-CP's BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST sets Activity Notification Level UE and carries no UE Inactivity Timer, which TS 37.483 9.2.2.1 says is "Included if the Activity Notification Level is set to UE". Our CU-UP never needed it (the CU-CP ran its own inactivity timer), so P1 never saw it. Found by the P2 code survey against OCUDU, whose CU-UP refuses the request (ocudu-fork d9d2263f4d lib/e1ap/cu_up/e1ap_cu_up_asn1_helpers.h). Fix in P2 Q4 (the timer) and Q5 (the CU-UP's inactivity notification, KS-E1AP-003). The timer fixed in P2 Q4: the request carries its activity level and, at "ue", the UE Inactivity Timer (IE 59, after the level; CuCpConfig ue_inactivity_s, 120 s); the builder refuses "ue" without one or a value outside 1..7200 | src/codec/asn1/msg/e1ap.cpp, the BearerContextSetupRequest builder; tests/unit E1apMsg.TheUeLevelCarriesTheUeInactivityTimer; P2 Q0 (found), Q4/Q5 (fix) |
| KS-E1AP-S2 | 2026-10-16 | TS 37.483 9.3.1.32 gives the UP keys as an unconstrained OCTET STRING "as defined in TS 33.501", which does not say whether that is the 128-bit algorithm key (TS 33.501 A.8: the n least significant bits of the KDF output) or the 256-bit KDF output. Our CU-CP sends the 128-bit algorithm key; OCUDU's CU-CP sends 256 bits. Our CU-UP takes either, a 256-bit key's 128 least significant bits being the algorithm key (A.8); OCUDU's CU-UP reads a 128-bit key as the first half of a 256-bit one (docs/interop/ocudu.md O-5) | src/proc/ran/cuup.cpp handle(BearerContextSetupRequest); P2 Q5 |
| KS-E1AP-B3 | 2026-10-16 | E1 additions of P2 Q5 (TS 37.483). The CU-UP's inactivity monitoring at activity level "ue" (8.3.1.2): the timer starts at the bearer context's setup and is restarted by any UL or DL user data; when it runs out, one BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION with UE-Activity not-active (8.6.3), again only after data. The CU-CP turns it into a UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with user-inactivity, as for a ksim-ctl release. The CU-CP's UE Inactivity Timer is a topology key (cucp: {ue_inactivity_s}), 7200 s by default so a gate's UEs are released only when it says; the E1 topologies set 15 s. The DRB's PDCP-Configuration now carries the CU-UP's DL discard timer, the one the UE gets in RRC ("infinity"), and t-Reordering when RRC sets one: OCUDU's CU-UP builds no DL PDCP entity without a discard timer (docs/interop/ocudu.md O-3). The codec reads the notification's UE-Activity choice only | src/proc/ran/cuup.cpp watch_inactivity(); src/proc/ran/cucp.cpp; src/codec/asn1/msg/e1ap.cpp; P2 Q5 |
